themes_detail.label: Tree Crisis in Crown Heights
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints spiked to 15 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.6 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 2300% increase (z-score: 29.69)—signaling either a sudden storm event, neglected maintenance, or a concentrated cluster of hazardous conditions affecting public safety and sidewalk access.
evidence: 15 tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Z-score of 29.69 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
Matches recurring CB budget request for park facility upgrades and tree maintenance—suggests chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Was there a weather event (wind, rain) that triggered fall/breakage, or is this evidence of years of deferred Parks Dept maintenance?
Geographic concentration: are complaints clustered in specific blocks or parks (Prospect Park edges, residential streets)?

themes_detail.label: Homeless Services Surge Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 26 LAST WEEK compared to a 2.9-per-week baseline—an 804% spike (z-score: 11.08)—reflecting either a sudden influx of unhoused individuals, a service gap, or a community reporting surge tied to winter weather or shelter capacity.
evidence: 26 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 2.9 weekly average (8-week baseline)
Community board has repeatedly requested expanded homeless services facilities (recurring budget request)
reporting_angles: Did a specific shelter close, reach capacity, or relocate? Interview DHS and local shelter operators.
Are complaints concentrated in commercial areas (Atlantic Ave, Prospect Park West) or residential blocks? Map the 311 complaints.
How is this comparing to citywide homeless trends—is Crown Heights disproportionately affected?

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Street/sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 81 LAST WEEK versus a 19.4-per-week baseline—a 318% increase (z-score: 4.79)—and commercial noise is up 100% from 3 weeks ago, suggesting either new construction activity, late-night venues, or street fairs that warrant enforcement review.
evidence: 81 street/sidewalk noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 19.4 weekly average
46 commercial noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 23.0 weekly average (100% spike)
483 active DOB building permits filed (282 alterations) suggest ongoing construction noise
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 noise complaints with active construction permits: are complaints clustering around active sites?
Interview residents on Nostrand Ave, Washington Ave, or other high-complaint streets about nightlife, street vendors, or events.
Are NYPD noise enforcement and DOE/Buildings compliance keeping pace with volume?

themes_detail.label: Maintenance and Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Maintenance or facility complaints surged to 15 THIS WEEK versus a 3.6-per-week baseline—a 314% spike (z-score: 6.09)—coinciding with street sign shortages (3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 average) and missing storm infrastructure, indicating accelerating neglect of public assets.
evidence: 15 maintenance/facility complaints THIS WEEK vs. 3.6 weekly average
Street sign complaints: 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Community board's recurring budget requests for 'other facilities' and catch basin cleaning suggest systemic underfunding
reporting_angles: Are these complaints tied to aging street furniture, park equipment, or subway infrastructure?
Interview Sanitation, Parks, and DOT to understand staffing and capital budget constraints.
Is there a specific neighborhood area showing concentration of complaints?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and Street Conditions Deteriorate
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints peaked at 12 three weeks ago—a 317% spike from the 2.9-per-week baseline (z-score: 3.94)—alongside elevated dead animal (380% spike) and unsanitary condition complaints (784 total over 90 days), pointing to neglected street maintenance and pest management.
evidence: Graffiti complaints: 12 (3 weeks ago) vs. 2.9 weekly average (317% spike)
Dead animal complaints: 6 (last week) vs. 1.2 weekly average (380% spike)
Unsanitary condition: 784 complaints over 90 days (baseline concern)
reporting_angles: Is this a symptom of understaffing at Sanitation or Parks enforcement?
Are specific blocks or parks becoming visible eyesores? Visual journalism opportunity.
Community board's recurring 'other cleaning requests' suggests Sanitation is not meeting demand.
